chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Recite the Quran with the tones of the Arabs and their voices; and beware of the tunes of the people of immorality and the people of major sins, for there will come after me groups of people who will repeat the Quran in the manner of songs, lamentation, and monasticism — it will not pass their throats. Their hearts are inverted, as are the hearts of those who are amazed by their conduct.'

key_terms.أَلْحَان: Tones, melodies, musical modes of recitation
key_terms.تَرَاقِي: Collarbones/throats — a Quranic metaphor for recitation that does not penetrate the heart
key_terms.لُحُون: Tunes, modes — here with negative connotation of improper melodic styles
key_terms.مَقْلُوبَة: Inverted, overturned — describes hearts that are spiritually corrupt and unable to receive guidance

ai.seo_question: How should the Quran be recited according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) commanded that the Quran be recited in the natural tones and voices of the Arabs, and warned against imitating the vocal styles of the immoral and sinful. He prophesied that future generations would recite the Quran like songs, lamentations, or monastic chanting, without the recitation penetrating their hearts — and both these reciters and those impressed by them would have inverted hearts. This warning came in the context of the early Muslim community, where the Prophet sought to preserve the authentic Arab manner of Quranic recitation and prevent its distortion through foreign or religiously corrupted vocal traditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Al Ahmad, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Abdulla Bin Sinan,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘

Recite the Quran with the tone of the Arabs and their voices; and beware of the immoral people and the people (committing) major sins, for there would be coming a group of people after me<sup>saww</sup>, they would be repeating (Verses) of the Quran like the repetition of the songs, and the lamentations, and the monks, not exceeding their throats. Their hearts would be inverted along with the hearts of the ones amazed by their affair’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ibrahim al-Ahmar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah  (a.s.) who has said the following: “Read the Holy Quran with Arabic accent and voice. You must not read it with the accent of the sinful people who commit major sins.

After me there will come people who will read the Holy Quran like singing, lamentations and in the monkish manner, which does not pass even their throats toward their hearts that are upside down and so are the hearts of those who like them.”
